transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 36 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Diego Martins (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Nova ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Nova Platform Eng), Ruth Park (Nova PO)
Shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/s/pocteam/cache-dashboard (dashboard), https://redwood.app/s/pocteam/kv-raw-logs (raw logs)

Summary (auto):
Quick sync on POC cache metrics; focused on prefix/KV cache hit rates, prompt reuse strategy changes, and immediate tuning steps to lift hit rate from current 18% to target ~45% for low-latency paths. Agreed to run additional 24h capture and push normalization changes to staging.

00:00 Alex Chen: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, let's just jump in, we got 36 minutes so quick agenda, cache hit overview, sample prompts, tuning plan, next steps
00:28 Maya Singh: yeah, thanks. quick note, ran another night run, we saw the overall token cost drop when caching kicked in but hit rate still pretty low, like 18-ish percent for prefix cache
00:46 Priya Rao: mm-hmm, we pulled the same window from our end, and the KV cache hit is 12% which matches the raw logs we shared, there are a lot of prompt mutations from the front-end that are preventing re-use
01:05 Tom Alvarez: those mutations are mostly user-ids and timestamps inserted in the prompt template, so even small changes break the prefix match
01:22 Diego Martins: yeah, common problem. We can apply prefix normalization and variable masking to improve match. Did you try the templating lib we suggested?
01:37 Maya Singh: we did try a naive regex replace, but it only caught a subset, also some of our templated content is derived at client side so tricky to normalize server-side
01:55 Priya Rao: got it. quick question — are you using session-affinity/sticky routing in the test cluster? that can improve KV cache reuse because the same model backend keeps the KV shards warm
02:10 Tom Alvarez: currently not sticky, we have stateless LB for scale tests. We can enable stickiness on the canary pool if that helps
02:25 Alex Chen: for this POC we'd recommend enabling sticky for the 4-node canary group. It usually raises KV reuse for short sessions. We estimate a 5-10% absolute lift from stickiness alone based on similar workloads
02:43 Maya Singh: ok let's try that. One other thing: our prompt variations include a product sku field and short descriptive sentence that varies a lot — that kills prefix reuse
03:05 Priya Rao: can you paste a few real prompts into the shared doc, with sensitive fields redacted? we can run a match simulation and show which patterns are breaking cache keys
03:20 Maya Singh: yes will do, i'll add 48 examples by tomorrow
03:32 Ruth Park: quick commercial question, are there risks if we normalize too aggressively and we lose context signals? i.e., will outputs degrade if we mask out too much
03:48 Diego Martins: good point. normalization has to be careful. we propose token-level masking rules: mask identifiers and timestamps, but keep short descriptors and product context intact. we also have fallback policy to bypass cache when match score low
04:10 Alex Chen: also important — the cache stores tokens + KV entries tied to model version; if you roll model variants during canary we need to keep pinning to same model or warm separately
04:25 Tom Alvarez: noted. our canary will be pinned to 1.2.1 for the next 48 hours
04:36 Priya Rao: ok, let's look at concrete numbers from this morning's capture. pulling up the dashboard, shared link...
04:50 [screen share sound, slight delay]
05:08 Priya Rao: so this window 02:00-06:00 UTC, total requests 24k, prefix cache hits 18%, KV hits 12%, cold starts 14% of calls leading to higher latency tails
05:28 Maya Singh: can you clarify cold start? is that model spin-up or KV miss causing full compute?
05:40 Priya Rao: principally KV miss + no cached attention states causing runtime to do full decode path — not a GPU spin-up. that explains the latency skew
05:55 Tom Alvarez: those tail latencies are what our SLO is sensitive to, anything over 500ms is triggering our alarms in staging
06:08 Priya Rao: in the sample, median latency 180ms when cache used, 620ms on KV miss; so lifting KV hit is critical for SLO
06:23 Maya Singh: makes sense. what's the distribution by route? some routes show 40% hits, others 3%
06:36 Priya Rao: yes, that's the skew. routes with more templated prompts had higher reuse. the problem routes are search-like free text where users paste long descriptions
06:50 Diego Martins: for free-text it's harder to prefix match. we can implement fuzzy prefix mapping: canonicalize whitespace, lowercasing, strip punctuation, and apply a simhash bucket for longer prompts to reuse partially
07:12 Maya Singh: simhash sounds heavy. what's the expected false positive risk if we bucket? could get wrong completions
07:24 Diego Martins: risk exists, so we suggest conservative bucket thresholds and always validate via a lightweight semantic-check — if the cached output passes a similarity threshold to the input, serve it, else regenerate
07:42 Ruth Park: will that add latency? extra similarity check sounds like more work
07:50 Priya Rao: the similarity check runs on a tiny embedding model (cheap) and is inline ~20ms, which is much cheaper than full decode. overall still net positive if it converts KV misses to hits
08:06 Tom Alvarez: what about cost impact? we need numbers for cost saving vs complexity
08:14 Alex Chen: based on our sim, raising KV hits from 12% to 45% reduces per-token GPU compute by approx 32% for your workload, cost-savings roughly 22% month-over-month at projected volume. We'll share the regression spreadsheet
08:33 Maya Singh: good. one hole we noticed — many prompts include user-specific examples they paste during debugging, which will never cache. can we detect dev-mode or long tail users and skip caching logic there?
08:49 Priya Rao: yes we can apply heuristics: user-agent or request header flags and prompt length thresholds to gate caching. we'll flag anything with 'debug' header or length <30 or >800 as no-cache by default
09:07 Tom Alvarez: that should help. next, about metrics: the dashboard shows "prefix_hit_rate" and "kv_hit_rate" — what's the exact key definition? there was confusion with your earlier naming in raw-logs
09:22 Priya Rao: sorry for the mismatch, here's the definitions: prefix_hit_rate = fraction of requests that matched a cached textual prefix and used cache; kv_hit_rate = fraction where the model KV/state reuse path was exercised. we'll rename fields in dashboard to be explicit and push notes to the doc
09:42 Maya Singh: please do, the team was reading them interchangeably
09:49 Alex Chen: ok action items: Priya will update normalization rules and push to staging; Diego will prototype simhash bucket logic in a sandbox; Alex will enable sticky routing on canary; Maya will provide 48 prompts; Tom will enable pinning to model 1.2.1
10:10 Ruth Park: any blockers around security? does caching touch PII?
10:18 Priya Rao: important note — cache keys do not store raw PII fields, we recommend hashing/redaction before keys created; default config in your deployment already redacts emails/SSNs but we'll validate and share proof
10:35 Maya Singh: can you show where in the logs the masking happened?
10:42 Priya Rao: yes, the raw log link has masked vs unmasked examples. we will also provide the config snippet: "redwood.cache.masking_rules": "email, ssn, creditcard" in the shared config repo
11:00 Alex Chen: ok timing — plan to push normalization changes by 2025-02-22 to staging, run 24h capture with sticky routing enabled starting 2025-02-23, then reconvene next Friday for results
11:20 Tom Alvarez: sounds good. Could we also run a 2-hour targeted bench with synthetic prompts to stress the simhash buckets?
11:30 Diego Martins: yes we can schedule that after the normalization push, we'll need the 48 sample prompts first to seed buckets
11:40 Maya Singh: i'll add the prompts and indicate which are dev/test vs prod examples
11:52 Alex Chen: cool. any last things?
12:00 Ruth Park: just please note compliance check — want to see KMS logs in case of forensics, we might ask for SOC2 artifact later
12:14 Priya Rao: understood, we'll put KMS access logs and masking proof in the security doc and share link
12:28 Alex Chen: thanks everyone. quick recap of next steps in the chat and action items in the doc. we'll follow up with meeting invite for perf deep dive

End transcript
